education.title: Mastering Phishing & Lookalike Domains
education.description: Learn how attackers craft spoofed URLs with homoglyphs, subdomains, and suspicious TLDs to mimic top Indian banks.
education.content: Phishing attacks rely on deceiving users into mistaking malicious websites for trusted institutions. Attackers use lookalike domains (e.g., sbl.com using 'l' instead of 'i'), subdomains (e.g., sbi.com.malicious-site.com), and urgent wording in SMS/Email to bypass suspicion.

quiz.question: You receive an SMS: 'Your bank account is locked. Update KYC at http://sbi.kyc-verification.top'. What is the primary indicator of fraud?
options: The domain uses .top and is not the official sbi.co.in website
The link opens in a web browser
quiz.explanation: Official State Bank of India portals operate on sbi.co.in or bank.sbi. Non-official TLDs like .top combined with subdomains are classic phishing setups.

education.title: Decoding Reverse UPI QR Code Fraud
education.description: Understand why entering a UPI PIN on a received QR code or collect request ALWAYS deducts money from your bank account.
education.content: A cardinal rule of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is: YOU ONLY NEED A PIN TO SEND MONEY, NEVER TO RECEIVE IT. Scammers on OLX or Telegram send 'Payment QR Codes' claiming scanning them will credit money into your account.

quiz.question: A buyer on OLX sends you a QR code claiming it will transfer Rs 5,000 into your account for an item. What happens if you scan and enter your UPI PIN?
options: Rs 5,000 will be credited into your account
Rs 5,000 will be DEDUCTED from your account
The payment request will be canceled
Your UPI app will automatically block the buyer
quiz.explanation: Entering your UPI PIN authorizes a payment OUT of your bank account. Scammers exploit this misunderstanding to steal funds.

education.title: OTP Protection & Screen Sharing Traps
education.description: How fraudsters trick users into sharing OTPs via fake customer support calls or AnyDesk/TeamViewer apps.
education.content: One-Time Passwords (OTPs) serve as the final line of defense for digital transactions. Fraudsters often pose as customer care executives or bank officials asking you to download remote access apps (AnyDesk, QuickSupport) or read out OTPs.

quiz.question: A caller claiming to be from customer support asks you to download 'AnyDesk' to fix a failed transaction refund. Should you proceed?
options: Yes, download it so they can fix the error
No, remote desktop apps allow attackers to view your screen and steal OTPs in real-time
Yes, but only if they give their employee ID
No, unless they promise a cashback bonus
quiz.explanation: Remote access tools grant full control over your smartphone screen. Scammers view incoming SMS OTPs and drain accounts instantly.
